note: Google's grade is numeric and company-wide (L3-L10): the company row, which pay and the Walk guide read. Each family titles the grade in its own words, and a family rung takes its band from that word or, when the title carries none ("Product Manager II"), from its grade on this row. Rungs measured from Google's posted base ranges, which are per grade: `pay_grades.py` holds the ranges and the titles that anchor each one.

Apple's ICT ladder is Individual Contributor TECHNICAL: valid inside engineering only. Its manager ladder: M1 is a first-line manager paid alongside ICT4, M2 with ICT5, M3 with ICT6; D1 is a director.

Amazon runs one company-wide L4-L12 ladder. "SDE III" is only the engineering TITLE at L6, so each engineering rung carries both its code and its title. SDE II (L5) is the mid rung and Senior SDE (L6) the senior one; there is no Staff rung and no IC L9.
Netflix ladders L3-L7 (its own codes are E3-E7); L7 is Principal and there is no L8.
OpenAI titles everyone Member of Technical Staff over hidden L2-L7.
Anthropic names its engineering rungs; other functions read the seniority word.

Nvidia's IC grades carry no engineering morpheme and read company-wide. Its seed pay is unconfirmed. Manager ladder M2-M5, one rung above the IC it manages. Its printed "Level 4" is family-relative, so it is deliberately not a printed code here.
Spotify's engineering ladder is named and tops out at Staff: there is no published Principal rung. Senior and Staff seeds are US medians.

Microsoft's number (59-70) is company-wide. 63 and 64 are both titled Senior, 65-67 all Principal, 68+ Partner; there is no Staff rung. Its postings also PRINT a track code ("Product Management IC5"). The calibration is pay-free: Microsoft's dual-rung reqs pair two titles with exactly two rungs ("Senior Product Manager / Product Manager" -> IC3 + IC4; "Senior and Principal Product Manager" -> IC4 + IC5; "Principal Product Manager" -> IC5 + IC6), so IC3 is the bare rung, IC4 Senior, and IC5 and IC6 both Principal. Single-rung postings agree. M and IC at the same number are the same rung on two tracks: M4/IC4, M5/IC5 and M6/IC6 post identical bands to the dollar. A posted pay band can exclude a rung but cannot locate one, which is why no pay fit enters this calibration.
The listing's own `careerLevel` field (raw_level; "Team Lead/Consultant" reads as its first part): the employer's statement, read before the title.

A rung printed in a public board field, banded only where postings whose title states the band agree on it (2+ anchors, 80%+ agreeing, the posted-range rule). A value the anchors did not settle is left out and the title decides: Reddit IC5, Waymo 4 and 8, SambaNova IC5/IC6, SharkNinja Lead and Manager.
